_comment: wp_pgp — keyless PGP keyserver pivot (e-mail / v4-v6 fingerprint / long key id -> public key(s) -> UIDs, creation times, subkeys, third-party certifiers). Every endpoint template, the Proton domain list and the algorithm-name tables live here (RULE 3) so a keyserver moving or a new algorithm id is a data edit, not a code change. `{email}`, `{fpr}`, `{keyid}` and `{search}` are URL-encoded by the caller before substitution. Nothing here is case data — public keyserver hostnames and RFC 4880 / RFC 9580 vocabulary only. RULE 5: an e-mail or name found in a key's UID is SELF-ASSERTED by whoever made the key (no keyserver except keys.openpgp.org verifies anything) — it is a LEAD, never an edge, never an operator.

settings._comment: timeout_seconds is the socket timeout per keyserver request. max_body_bytes caps how much of a response is parsed (popular keys on HKP servers carry thousands of certifications); anything beyond is truncated and flagged. max_certifiers_per_uid caps the third-party certifier list emitted per UID so a heavily-signed key does not flood the output.

sources._comment: Queried in this order. `kind` is 'vks' (keys.openpgp.org Verifying Key Service: returns ONE armored key, 404 when absent, and strips every UID whose e-mail the owner has not verified — so a key found by fingerprint may legitimately carry no UID) or 'hkp' (classic HKP: `get` returns armored key(s), `index` with options=mr returns machine-readable pub:/uid: lines). `by_*` keys are templates per selector type; a missing template means the source cannot answer that selector type and it is reported as skipped. `only_email_domains` restricts a source to e-mail selectors on those domains (Proton's HKP only knows Proton-hosted addresses). `account_age_proxy` marks a source whose primary-key creation time approximates mailbox creation. `serves_decoy_keys` marks a source that answers NON-EXISTENT addresses with a well-formed key carrying a plausible past creation date (Proton does this as anti-enumeration — observed 2026-11: random 20-hex local parts on proton.me/pm.me all return 200 + a key, stable across repeats); for such a source the age is reported `rung: unverified` unless a UID is certified by one of `ca_signer_uids` (the Signer's User ID subpacket of a third-party certification by the provider's own CA key — a vendor address, not case data).

pubkey_algorithms._comment: RFC 9580 §9.1 public-key algorithm ids -> short name.

curve_oids._comment: Hex of the DER OID body (without tag/length) carried in ECDH/ECDSA/EdDSA key material -> curve name (RFC 9580 §9.2).

fixed_key_bits._comment: Algorithms with a fixed key size and no curve OID (RFC 9580 v6 native key types).

key_flags._comment: Key Flags subpacket (type 27) bit -> usage letter, gpg-style.
